If you are already established in the industry you could look into consulting gigs. This can be especially lucrative if you have a skill set that is niched or hard to acquire. I suspect the lack of part-time staffed engineering gigs has something to do with the "mythical man-month" (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Mythical_Man-Month) which basically states adding more people grows the cost of overhead/communication. Meaning it is better to have fewer programmers work longer hours than more programmers working part time.

If you have a good history you could go freelance, other than that companies are generally not ready to let a developer work on important/technical things only part-time. It could happen, but unless you have good experience (3+ years), HR isn't even going to read your cover letter, and you will be considered just like a graduate fresh out of college.

Yes, you can definitely do it if you find companies that have a constant stream of jobs and regularly hire you as a freelancer. You'll somehow need to make connections in the area you want to work in.

Once they know they can rely on you, they'll prefer to work with you over other freelancers.
You may have better luck transitioning into testing. There's a better shot that people would be okay with a part-time tester vs a dev.

You will just be leaving money on the table by not working full time, but if you can support yourself on $20k and not strapped for cash then sure you could. I work as a part time developer 2 hours a day (10 hours a week) for another company while working my full time.. It's pretty nice having an extra $400/week in my pocket
